name: Small list
expr: (lambda a: [heapify(a), all(a[(i - 1) // 2] <= a[i] for i in range(1, len(a))), sorted(a) == sorted(args[0])][1:])(list(args[0]))
show: heapify [5, 3, 8, 1, 9, 2]: [is it now a min-heap?, same values?]
why: After heapify(a), every a[i] must be at least its parent a[(i - 1) // 2]. Work in place: change the list you were given, and return nothing.

name: Empty and one
why: Nothing to do: [] and [7]. Lists of length 0 and 1 are already heaps.

name: Already a heap
expr: (lambda a: [heapify(a), all(a[(i - 1) // 2] <= a[i] for i in range(1, len(a))), sorted(a) == sorted(args[0])][1:])(list(args[0]))
why: A sorted list is already a min-heap, and stays one.

name: Decreasing
expr: (lambda a: [heapify(a), all(a[(i - 1) // 2] <= a[i] for i in range(1, len(a))), sorted(a) == sorted(args[0])][1:])(list(args[0]))
why: Every value has to move. Sift down from the last parent, position n // 2 − 1, back to the root.

name: Repeated values
expr: (lambda a: [heapify(a), all(a[(i - 1) // 2] <= a[i] for i in range(1, len(a))), sorted(a) == sorted(args[0])][1:])(list(args[0]))
why: Equal values may stay in either order; only the parent ≤ child rule matters.

name: Kept in place
show: heapify [4, 1, 3], then read a[0] from the same list
why: The smallest value, 1, must be at a[0] of the list you were given. If you built a new list, the caller never sees it.

name: Comparisons, decreasing
expr: (lambda a: [heapify(a), comparisons() <= 3 * len(a), (lambda a: all(a[(i - 1) // 2] <= a[i] for i in range(1, len(a))))(plain(a))][1:])(counted(args[0]))
show: heapify 10,000 values from 10,000 down to 1: [at most 3n comparisons?, a heap?]
why: Sifting down from the middle costs fewer than 2n comparisons (lesson 3). Pushing the values one at a time and sifting each one up costs about n log₂ n here, around 110,000, because every new value moves up to the root.

name: Comparisons, mixed
expr: (lambda a: [heapify(a), comparisons() <= 3 * len(a), (lambda a: all(a[(i - 1) // 2] <= a[i] for i in range(1, len(a))))(plain(a))][1:])(counted(args[0]))
show: heapify 10,000 values in a mixed order: [at most 3n comparisons?, a heap?]

name: 200,000 values
expr: (lambda a: [heapify(a), a[0], all(a[(i - 1) // 2] <= a[i] for i in range(1, len(a)))][1:])(list(args[0]))
why: O(n) work. If this timed out, the code may sort, or copy slices of the list inside the loop.
